journal.text: Opening session, no prior positions. Building a diversified core in mega-cap tech leaders with strong secular growth exposure: AI/semis (NVDA, AVGO), cloud/software (MSFT, GOOGL), consumer/ads (AMZN, META), plus AAPL for stability and COST as a defensive quality name. Sized roughly by conviction and recent momentum, keeping ~$2k cash buffer. NVDA and AVGO have strong AI capex tailwinds; MSFT/GOOGL have cloud+AI monetization; AMZN/META are re-accelerating; AAPL is a stable anchor; COST is a quality defensive holding despite recent dip. Will reassess as earnings season approaches in mid-October and rebalance based on price action, especially watching AVGO/NVDA volatility around AI capex headlines and any weakness in COST after its post-earnings drop. Will trim laggards or add to winners as trends confirm over the next few sessions.

Will reassess as October earnings season approaches, particularly watching AVGO/NVDA around AI capex headlines, COST post-earnings recovery, and any weakness in AMZN/META that might warrant trimming or adding. Will reassess as October earnings season begins (particularly AVGO, COST, and NVDA around AI capex commentary) and watch for COST to show signs of stabilizing or further deterioration before deciding to trim.

Ninth session, no trades. Oct 10 saw a sharp broad-based selloff across all core holdings on elevated volume: NVDA -4.9% to 183.16, MSFT -2.2% to 510.96, GOOGL -2.1% to 236.57, AVGO -5.9% to 324.63, AAPL -3.4% to 245.27, AMZN -5.0% to 216.37, META -3.8% to 705.30, COST -1.4% to 930.01. This looks like a single-day macro/risk-off event (uniform decline across uncorrelated sectors - semis, retail, cloud, social) rather than any stock-specific fundamental breakdown - no earnings misses or company-specific news driving this. Wide intraday ranges (e.g., NVDA low 182.05 vs high 195.62, AMZN low 216 vs high 228.25) suggest a volatility spike/flush rather than a trend change. All positions remain within or near recent multi-week ranges; none have broken key support decisively with follow-through. Selling into a one-day flush without a clear catalyst would lock in losses on a diversified mega-cap book that has performed well YTD. Holding current allocation unchanged with ~$2k cash buffer. Will reassess next session: if the selloff continues with a second down day and volume confirmation (especially META below 700 or NVDA below 180 with follow-through), will consider trimming. If it's a one-day flush, expect partial recovery.

Tenth session, no trades. All positions recovered meaningfully from Oct 10 lows, validating the thesis that it was a volatility flush rather than trend change. No position broke key support with follow-through (META held above 700, NVDA held above 180). Maintaining diversified mega-cap tech core unchanged with ~$2k cash buffer. Will continue monitoring Q3 earnings season (AVGO/NVDA capex commentary, big tech earnings starting late Oct) and reassess if any position shows a genuine breakdown with volume confirmation below recent support levels.

Twenty-second session, no trades. Data still observed through Oct 29 close (NVDA 207.04, MSFT 541.55, GOOGL 274.57, AVGO 385.98, AAPL 269.70, AMZN 230.30, META 751.67, COST 912.42). MSFT/GOOGL/META reported Q3 earnings after the Oct 29 close - their market reaction will only show up in today's Oct 30 open, which is unobservable to us before order execution. AMZN reports after today's close, so its reaction will land tomorrow. Since today's open already prices in overnight earnings moves we cannot see or anticipate, there's no informational edge to act on now - better to let the reaction land and reassess with real post-earnings data next session rather than gamble on direction. GOOGL and AVGO/NVDA already show strong momentum into earnings (GOOGL +8% and AVGO +9% over the past week), while COST continues to drift lower (932->912, no catalyst, just soft mega-cap retail sentiment) - worth watching COST for a possible trim if the downtrend persists post-reaction. Cash remains ~$2k, net worth ~$54.2k, portfolio unchanged: NVDA, MSFT, GOOGL, AVGO, AAPL, AMZN, META, COST mega-cap tech core. Will reassess capex/guidance commentary and price reaction magnitude once real post-earnings closes are observed tomorrow.

Twenty-third session, no trades. Data now observed through Oct 30 close, so META's earnings reaction is visible: META gapped down -11% at Oct 30 open (751.67->669.15 open, closed 666.47) on capex/spending guidance concerns - a large, already-priced-in move we can't act on retroactively. MSFT's reaction was milder (-3% from 541.55 to 525.76). GOOGL's reaction was strongly positive: gapped up +6% at open (274.57->291.59) and closed 281.48, extending its pre-earnings rally. AMZN reported after the Oct 30 close, so its market reaction lands at today's (Oct 31) open, which remains unobservable to us before order execution - holding through this final earnings catalyst rather than guessing direction. NVDA, AVGO, AAPL, COST show no unusual catalyst-driven moves, just normal drift (COST still soft, ~920, down modestly from 936 two weeks ago - continuing to watch but not yet a clear trend break worth trimming for). Cash ~$2k, net worth ~$53.1k. Since META's move is now fully reflected in current values and AMZN's reaction is still unknown, there's no actionable edge today - will reassess AMZN's post-earnings price action and whether META's selloff presents a buying opportunity or confirms a deteriorating capex-spend narrative once tomorrow's close is observed.

Monthly $50k deposit landed, pushing cash to ~$52k (>50% of net worth) - too much idle capital sitting out of the market. All October earnings reactions are now fully observed and priced in: META's -11% capex-guidance selloff (now 648, down from 751 pre-earnings) looks overdone for a business still growing ad revenue at scale, so adding on weakness as a mean-reversion/value bet. AMZN's post-earnings pop (+9.6% gap on Oct 31, 222.86->244.22) confirms a strong AWS/margin beat - adding to ride confirmed momentum rather than chasing pre-reaction. GOOGL and COST get modest top-ups: GOOGL for continued Cloud strength post its +6% earnings gap, COST as a mean-reversion nibble after a soft two-week drift (936->911) with no negative catalyst, just sentiment. Deploying the rest of the cash into new diversifying positions to reduce concentration risk in the existing 8-name mega-cap tech cluster: AMD and MU add semiconductor/memory cyclical exposure (memory pricing cycle turning, AMD data-center GPU narrative), CRWD and PANW add cybersecurity exposure, a sector with different demand drivers than AI capex names. Keeping ~$11k cash buffer for flexibility. Will reassess sizing and reconsider trims if new positions show sustained weakness, or add further if the semis/security allocation proves too light relative to the mega-cap core.

Twenty-fifth session, no trades. Yesterday's deploy-cash session addressed the excess cash balance (added to META/AMZN/GOOGL/COST, opened AMD/MU/CRWD/PANW), bringing cash to ~$11k (~10.6% of $103.4k net worth) - a reasonable buffer, not excessive. Reviewing today's data (through Nov 3 close): no new earnings catalysts pending for this basket. META continues to stabilize post-selloff (648->638, still digesting capex guidance, no fresh info to act on). AMZN holding gains from the AWS beat (254, up from 230 pre-earnings). GOOGL steady near highs (284). AAPL, MSFT drifting sideways with no signal. New semis (AMD, MU) and security (CRWD, PANW) positions are one day old - too early to judge, will give them time to develop before adjusting. COST recovered to 928 from its recent dip, validating the mean-reversion nibble. No compelling new entry or exit signal today - holding all positions unchanged. Will reassess if COST or META show renewed weakness, if AMD/MU/CRWD/PANW show sustained trend confirmation (add) or breakdown (trim), or if cash buffer drifts too high/low relative to net worth.

Twenty-sixth session, no trades. Nov 4 close data shows a broad-based, market-wide pullback hitting nearly every holding simultaneously: NVDA -4%, MSFT -0.5%, GOOGL -2.2%, AVGO -2.9%, AMZN -2.1%, META -1.5%, AMD -3.7%, MU -7.1%, CRWD -3.3%, PANW -2.1%. Only COST and AAPL held up (COST actually up to 940 from 928, AAPL flat ~270). This pattern - a synchronized decline across mega-cap tech, semis, and security names on the same day - looks like a macro/risk-off move (broader tech de-rating) rather than any stock-specific breakdown in fundamentals. No earnings, guidance, or company-specific news distinguishes the losers from each other; COST's relative strength (a staple/value name) is consistent with this being risk-off rotation rather than a signal to trim growth positions. Since there's no differentiated evidence that any single name's thesis has broken (vs. just a bad tape day), and my new semis/security positions (AMD, MU, CRWD, PANW, now 2 sessions old) don't yet have enough data to judge trend, I'm holding everything unchanged rather than reacting to one day of broad weakness. Cash ~$11k (~11% of NW) remains an adequate buffer. Will reassess if the weakness persists/accelerates over the next 2-3 sessions (which would suggest a real regime shift worth trimming into), or if it reverses quickly (confirming today was noise, possibly worth adding to the dip on names like MU/AMD that fell hardest with no distinct bad news).

Twenty-seventh session, no trades. Reviewed 5-day price history through Nov 5 close to check whether the Nov 4 broad tech pullback was a one-day macro air-pocket or the start of a trend. Result is mixed/reassuring: GOOGL (277.5->284.3), MU (218->237.5, +8.9%), AMD (250->256.3), COST (940.7->935, still elevated vs pre-dip 911), and AAPL (flat ~270) all bounced or held on Nov 5, consistent with my prior read that Nov 4 was broad risk-off noise, not a fundamental breakdown. However NVDA continued lower (198.7 from 202.5, now well off its 206-208 range from Oct 30-31), MSFT drifted down again (514->507), and CRWD/PANW stayed soft (534/213, still below their Oct 30 levels). So the picture is a partial recovery in semis/memory/search/staples but continued weakness in NVDA specifically and in the two security names. None of these have a distinct negative catalyst (no earnings in this window) - just relative price action. Given the mixed signal (some names confirming 'buy the dip' thesis, others still soft) and no new information to differentiate causes, I'm holding all positions unchanged rather than trading on ambiguous short-term noise. Cash ~$11k (~11% of NW) remains an adequate buffer. Will reassess NVDA and CRWD/PANW specifically if their relative underperformance persists another session or two (possible trim candidates), and would consider adding to MU/AMD/GOOGL if their rebound continues with volume confirmation.

Twenty-eighth session. The broad tech weakness I first flagged as possibly macro noise on Nov 4 has now persisted for three consecutive sessions (Nov 4-6) in several of my highest-beta names: NVDA fell 208->188 (-9.6% in a week, new local low, no bounce), AMD 259->237.7 (-8.5%, gave back all of its Nov 5 bounce), CRWD stayed soft (534->532, below its late-Oct range), and PANW continued lower (220->211, -8.9% in a week). This is exactly the 'persists another session or two' trigger I set in my last two journals for trimming rather than holding through. Meanwhile GOOGL, AMZN, and COST have shown relative resilience/recovery, and MSFT/META, while also down, are large diversified compounders I'm keeping full-sized. So I'm taking a targeted risk-reduction action: trimming ~20% of the NVDA, AMD, CRWD, and PANW positions (my four weakest, most volatile names with no offsetting bounce) to raise cash from ~11% to ~16-17% of net worth. This isn't a full exit - I still believe in the AI/semis/security theses long-term - but the multi-day confirmed downtrend in these specific names, unaccompanied by any stabilizing catalyst, warrants reducing size rather than continuing to hold at full weight or averaging down blindly. Will reassess for re-entry if these names stabilize/reverse with volume, or continue trimming further if the downtrend broadens to GOOGL/AMZN/COST (which would signal a true regime shift vs. idiosyncratic high-beta unwind).

Twenty-ninth session. Price history through Nov 7 close is identical to what informed my Nov 7 trim decision (no new session data available - Nov 10 is the next trading day after a Fri Nov 7 close, weekend gap). Since I already executed the targeted trim of NVDA/AMD/CRWD/PANW on Nov 7 to raise cash to ~16% of NW, and there's no new price action to react to, I'm holding all positions unchanged today rather than trading on stale information. Quick scan of the trailing data: CRWD (532.5->539.8) and PANW (211.4->212.3) showed small bounces on Nov 7, a tentative stabilization signal; AMD kept sliding (237.7->233.5) with no bounce, remaining the weakest name; NVDA also ticked up marginally (188.08->188.15) after its steep multi-day decline. MSFT continues to drift lower (497.1->496.8) without a distinct catalyst. Nothing here overrides the trim thesis or argues for re-entry yet. Will look for a fresh, confirmed multi-day bounce with volume in NVDA/AMD/CRWD/PANW before redeploying the ~16% cash buffer, or continue trimming AMD specifically if its lone-wolf downtrend (now diverging from CRWD/PANW's stabilization) persists into new sessions.

Thirtieth session. New data point: Nov 10 close showed a broad, synchronized bounce across nearly every holding - NVDA +5.8% (188.1->199.1), MU +6.5% (237.9->253.3), GOOGL +4.1% (278.8->290.1), AMD +4.5% (233.5->244.0), CRWD +3.3% (539.8->557.5), PANW +2.0% (212.3->216.5), AVGO +2.6%, MSFT +1.8%, AMZN +1.6%, META +1.6%, COST +0.85% (only laggard). Volume was healthy on the bounce names (NVDA, MU, AMD all above their recent average). This is the first genuinely broad-based, volume-confirmed up day since the Nov 4-7 selloff, and it touches essentially every position in the book, not just an idiosyncratic name. However, it is only ONE session of confirmation - my stated trigger for redeploying the ~16% cash buffer was a 'fresh, confirmed multi-day bounce,' and I don't yet have a second day to validate this isn't a one-day dead-cat bounce/short squeeze after a sharp multi-day decline. Given the account is not under any pressure (cash buffer of ~$15.8k, ~15.5% of NW, is comfortable, not distressed), the disciplined move is to hold unchanged again today and use tomorrow's session to check for follow-through. If Nov 11 confirms with a second up day (especially in NVDA/MU/GOOGL/AMD, the strongest bouncers), I will redeploy a portion of the cash buffer into those names.
